newsitem.title: USA: Fla. near ruling on tobacco trial plan.
newsitem.headline: Fla. near ruling on tobacco trial plan.

text.p: A Florida judge said Thursday he expected to issue an order within about a week on a trial plan for a class action suit brought against the tobacco industry on behalf of smokers in Florida.

"I am going to try to come up with an order sometime in the next week," said Dade Circuit Judge Alan Postman at a pre-trial hearing for the case known as Engle vs. R.J. Reynolds Tobacco, RJR Nabisco, Philip Morris Cos Inc et al. Postman also said he planned to take a vacation July 24-August 11, but that he still intended the trial to begin on September 8.

During the hearing, Robert Heim, co-counsel for Philip Morris, argued the trial should begin by asking the jury to determine whether or not tobacco is addictive. Stanley Rosenblatt, attorney for the plaintiffs, argued the trial should begin with a determination of liability and punitive damages.

Attorneys for Dow Jones & Co attended the hearing and asked the judge to be allowed to argue if the tobacco industry should seek a gag order in connection with the case. The judge said he would not rule on the request until such an order was actually sought.
